bug_semantics: POST /permission accepted a user-controlled roles[<role_id>][] map and PermissionSaveController::save() iterated it, calling Role::findById($role_id)->syncPermissions($permissions) without checking whether the caller was allowed to administer permissions or the selected role. After authentication was added, any authenticated low-privilege user could target their own or another role and assign the application's complete permission set, producing vertical privilege escalation.
flaw_origin: The smallest causal change is pull-request member commit b0fa7751b112038cb01a0fac3b2ab841f2f7f7cc: it simultaneously created app/Http/Controllers/Permission/PermissionSaveController.php with the generic Request-to-syncPermissions data flow and exposed it through an unguarded POST /permission route in routes/web.php. GitHub later squash-merged the two-member pull request as ac1919b745e0fd22973853954e8c92b1393f0920; the second member only applied unrelated Pint changes. Commit 52e5e1938ba7db9191ab75fc6f81d92cf667dd4d later made the controller inherit MainController, adding auth and locked middleware but leaving the missing role/permission-administration authorization and vulnerable sync logic intact.
ai_marker: absent — the exact BIC commit object names author Antonio <elguitarraverde@hotmail.com> and committer Antonio <elguitarraverde@hotmail.com>; its message is only 'feat(permission): add permissions dashboard' and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, other AI trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: Authoritative CNA advisory: https://secur0.com/en/cna/cve-list/cve-2026-59233-missing-authorization-in-prospero-flow-crm-permission-endpoint identifies app/Http/Controllers/Permission/PermissionSaveController.php, POST /permission, the attacker-controlled roles[<role_id>][] array, the direct syncPermissions call, affected versions before 5.2.1, introducer ac1919b7, and fix 86a7d655. GitHub's advisory is https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4fxp-2m36-qv64.

The first-party PR history at https://github.com/Roskus/prospero-flow-crm/pull/169 and https://api.github.com/repos/Roskus/prospero-flow-crm/pulls/169/commits exposes two pre-squash members: b0fa7751b112038cb01a0fac3b2ab841f2f7f7cc (feature implementation, parent 3a2916b5724679e3c1fac3b77c59c780b2e6ff74) and e6c0016d94c9775defeac4acfe5fa44c0ffc4fb5 (Pint only). git show --stat confirms b0fa7751 created the permission controllers, view, setting link, and routes, while e6c0016 changed only app/Http/Requests/ProductRequest.php and database/migrations/2023_03_24_112907_alter_product_add_tax_column.php.

git rev-parse ac1919b745e0fd22973853954e8c92b1393f0920^{tree} e6c0016d94c9775defeac4acfe5fa44c0ffc4fb5^{tree} returned the identical tree b5413915c08612442d106664734608e7f495e461 for both, proving ac1919b745e0fd22973853954e8c92b1393f0920 is the aggregate squash result; b0fa7751 is therefore the smaller causal BIC rather than the squash commit.

git show b0fa7751b112038cb01a0fac3b2ab841f2f7f7cc shows app/Http/Controllers/Permission/PermissionSaveController.php created with save(Request $request), $roles = $request->roles, and Role::findById($role_id)->syncPermissions($permissions), plus routes/web.php created with Route::post('/permission', ... 'save') and no can() or permission middleware.

Direct-parent verification: git rev-parse b0fa7751b112038cb01a0fac3b2ab841f2f7f7cc^ returned 3a2916b5724679e3c1fac3b77c59c780b2e6ff74; git ls-tree -r that parent for app/Http/Controllers/Permission/PermissionSaveController.php returned no entry, and git grep for Route::post('/permission' in that parent's routes/web.php returned no match. The vulnerable controller, route, and data flow are absent from the immediate parent tree.

History cross-check: git log 86a7d6557bd111518a221f4575ad6e36087e19d3^ -L 14,22:app/Http/Controllers/Permission/PermissionSaveController.php traces the vulnerable save method to squash ac1919b745e0fd22973853954e8c92b1393f0920; git log --all -S 'Role::findById($role_id)->syncPermissions($permissions);' finds only its addition at ac1919b745e0fd22973853954e8c92b1393f0920 and removal at fix 86a7d6557bd111518a221f4575ad6e36087e19d3. PR-member decomposition then locates the original addition in b0fa7751b112038cb01a0fac3b2ab841f2f7f7cc.

Lifecycle check: git show 52e5e1938ba7db9191ab75fc6f81d92cf667dd4d for PermissionSaveController changes only Controller to MainController. At the fix parent, MainController::middleware() supplies auth and locked, while routes/web.php lines 140-141 still expose GET and POST /permission without an authorization gate and PermissionSaveController still directly synchronizes request input. Thus 52e5e193 narrowed exploitation to authenticated users but did not create or repair the underlying missing authorization flaw.

Version-boundary check: b0fa7751b112038cb01a0fac3b2ab841f2f7f7cc contains APP_VERSION 2.2.11. git tag --contains ac1919b745e0fd22973853954e8c92b1393f0920 lists v1.0.0, v2.0.1, v4.6.0, v5.5.3, and v5.14.0; git grep at v1.0.0, v2.0.1, and v4.6.0 finds the vulnerable syncPermissions statement in PermissionSaveController.php line 19, proving vulnerable tagged releases. The unusual tag numbering does not change ancestry or source presence.

Direct fix evidence: https://github.com/Roskus/prospero-flow-crm/commit/86a7d6557bd111518a221f4575ad6e36087e19d3 and local git show demonstrate that 86a7d6557bd111518a221f4575ad6e36087e19d3 replaces generic Request with new PermissionSaveRequest, whose authorize() requires hasRole('SuperAdmin'), uses validated roles, and bumps APP_VERSION from 5.2.0 to 5.2.1. This directly closes the authorization path, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are the same commit.

Fixed-boundary check: no v5.2.1 tag exists. git tag --contains 86a7d6557bd111518a221f4575ad6e36087e19d3 lists v5.5.3 and v5.14.0; git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms the fix is an ancestor of v5.5.3, whose full commit is 584f315878b8366244c95fe3cb016b3a63f05db8, and git grep at v5.5.3 finds the SuperAdmin role authorization in app/Http/Requests/PermissionSaveRequest.php. The first tagged fixed release is therefore v5.5.3, matching https://github.com/Roskus/prospero-flow-crm/releases/tag/v5.5.3.

BIC-only AI check: numactl-prefixed git cat-file commit b0fa7751b112038cb01a0fac3b2ab841f2f7f7cc shows human author and committer Antonio <elguitarraverde@hotmail.com>, a one-line feature message, and no trailers. No later squash, authentication hardening, or fix attribution was used to attribute the BIC.
reasoning: The vulnerable behavior is the unmediated authority to rewrite any role's permission set, not merely the endpoint's authentication state. Member commit b0fa7751b112038cb01a0fac3b2ab841f2f7f7cc first created both the externally reachable POST route and the generic-request loop that applies attacker-selected permissions to attacker-selected role IDs. Its immediate parent has neither the controller file nor route. The mainline squash ac1919b745e0fd22973853954e8c92b1393f0920 preserved the two-member PR's final tree, but b0fa7751 is the smallest reconstructable causal commit; e6c0016 is unrelated formatting. Later commit 52e5e1938ba7db9191ab75fc6f81d92cf667dd4d added authentication while preserving the flawed authorization/data flow, yielding the advisory's low-privilege authenticated attack path. Commit 86a7d6557bd111518a221f4575ad6e36087e19d3 directly fixes that path by requiring a SuperAdmin-authorized FormRequest and validated input and marks version 5.2.1; the fix is present in the first containing tag v5.5.3. Because the exact smallest BIC commit object has only human author/committer identities and no AI marker, the causal verdict is NOT_AI even though later lifecycle commits are irrelevant to BIC attribution.
